Messages.Author: Mark Lamutt
Messages.Body:
Ok, I have no doubt this has been discussed to death, but I have to ask
anyway as it came up in our group over the weekend, and I didn't have a
good answer...

Minor Boon text:

Prevent a vampire controlled by another Methuselah
from going into torpor. Put this card on the vampire;
the vampire remains in the active region. In return,
that vampire cannot bleed you until it rescues a vampire
you control from torpor. This Minor Boon is then
burned.

After searching past articles on deja-news, I see that minor boon is
player after combat, but how do you prevent the vamp from going to
torpor? If you play the card, is the vamp automatically saved - ie does
the act of playing the card keep the vamp from going to torpor? Do you
pay the blood to heal the damage out of your pool? Does one of your
vamps pay for the damage?

Thanks,
Mark

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Mark Lamutt wrote:
> Minor Boon text:
>
> Prevent a vampire controlled by another Methuselah
> from going into torpor. Put this card on the vampire;
> the vampire remains in the active region. In return,
> that vampire cannot bleed you until it rescues a vampire
> you control from torpor. This Minor Boon is then
> burned.
>

> [...] how do you prevent the vamp from going to

> torpor? If you play the card, is the vamp automatically saved - ie does
> the act of playing the card keep the vamp from going to torpor? Do you
> pay the blood to heal the damage out of your pool? Does one of your
> vamps pay for the damage?

The vamp is "saved" by the effect of the Minor Boon. No other cost
need be paid to prevent him from going to torpor.
